items.title: Sherrie Maricle interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 18, 2001 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: And there was a concert with Maurice and I was just hired to play drums.

ctx.x: Do you think people would — I’m not sure how to even ask this — how would it change the look or the perception of your band if there was like three men in it?

We have had some men play with us. Sometimes, just by the nature — the band is at the highest professional level and there aren’t enough women to fill the chairs sometimes. So it’s not a problem with us. But like there’s always the argument of, “well if you’re all so good why do you have to play with each other?” which is kind of insulting. It’s like well, they why don’t you force — and I don’t agree with the issue of like forcing Wynton— there was a big article in the paper about trying to force Wynton Marsalis…
were all like oh, uh oh, I’m sitting next to like five other people who play just as good as I do who are my same gender. I’m not unique anymore. So it was really, really interesting.

I was in Cedar Rapids, Iowa at Coe College. I was on a little solo tour, like I was in Nebraska at the Nebraska Band Master’s Association.
